note: Window agent corrections for 2020-2029: the Russian occupation of Crimea and the south of Ukraine (the compiler closed the whole relation at the first occupation_end of 2022), Western Sahara roles for Dakhla and the Free Zone, the Rio Grande strip and Iraq's ownerless cells inherited from earlier windows, and the Uzbek-Kyrgyz one-cell border band.

intersect.text: north-west of the Dnieper and the Kakhovka reservoir (the line through the gazetteer's Dnieper cells): the right bank
the northern part of the oblast, north of 47.5 N, with the city of Zaporizhzhia (about 30 percent of the oblast)

region.text: Crimea and Sevastopol, and the occupied south: Kherson Oblast without the right bank of the Dnieper that Russia left on 9-11 November 2022, and Zaporizhzhia Oblast without its northern part with the city of Zaporizhzhia (about 30 percent), which stayed under Ukraine

events.note: Russia still held Crimea and Sevastopol (occupied since 2014) and the parts of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia oblasts (since 2022) at the end of 2022: the Russian-occupied territories page lists them as 'Russia (2014-present)' and 'Russia (2022-present)'. The compiler gives all Russian occupations of Ukraine one relation, and the first occupation_end (the Kyiv-area withdrawal of April 2022, /ledger/17) closed the whole relation, so Crimea and the south were drawn as plain Ukrainian land from 2022 on. This reopens the relation at the end of the year with the land the ledger itself carries (/ledger/13 Crimea; /ledger/14 Kherson and Zaporizhzhia, less the right bank of /ledger/21). Zaporizhzhia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaporizhzhia_Oblast): 'At that time, Russia was only in control of about 70% of the province's land area ... the northern parts of the oblast, including its capital city, Zaporizhzhia, remained under Ukrainian control'; the 45 km circle round the city is the cautious part of that 30%. Reviewer correction (p2020-p2029 review): the right bank is now cut along the Dnieper itself; the circles copied from /ledger/21 cut 9 left-bank cells round Oleshky and Hola Prystan out of the occupation and left 11 right-bank cells (Beryslav and Vysokopillia country) in it, while https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Kherson_counteroffensive says 'Russia announced the withdrawal of its troops from Kherson and the right bank of the Dnieper' and keeps 'Russian positions on the left bank'. The 45 km circle left Russia 85 percent of Zaporizhzhia Oblast against the page's 'about 70%'; the cut is now the oblast north of 47.5 N (32 of 111 cells, with the capital), so about 70 percent stays occupied.

region.text: the Free Zone east of the berm (the gazetteer's 'W. Sahara') and the Oued ed-Dahab (Dakhla) unit, the southern part of the territory that Morocco administers

events.note: 'Approximately 30% of the Western Sahara is controlled by the Polisario Front and the remaining 70% is occupied by Morocco'; 'The Polisario Front claims to run this as the Free Zone on behalf of the SADR.' The start anchor of 2020 still gives Morocco the whole Free Zone (330 cells) and 226 of the 273 Oued ed-Dahab cells, with SADR drawn as the occupier of the Moroccan-held Dakhla. The land is the SADR's: the Free Zone it holds, and Dakhla, which Morocco occupies (next entry, as for the Laayoune and Smara units).

region.text: Oued ed-Dahab (Dakhla), west of the berm

events.note: 'the remaining 70% is occupied by Morocco' (the territory west of the berm, with all the major cities). The Laayoune and Smara units are already drawn as SADR land occupied by Morocco; the Oued ed-Dahab unit was drawn the other way round (Moroccan land occupied by the SADR) in the 2020 anchor. Month 2 so that it follows the previous entry.

region.text: the United States side of the Rio Grande within 5 km (New Mexico, Texas, Colorado): US land that Mexico's 2009 gain 'six islands in the Rio Grande' took with a 5 km river strip

events.note: 24 November 2009: 'the U.S. ceded 6 islands in the Rio Grande to Mexico' while 'Mexico ceded 3 islands and 2 bancos to the U.S.'; the page gives no area and 'the continental border then follows the middle of the Rio Grande'. mexico /ledger/9 resolves the islands as the Rio Grande plus 5 km, which gave Mexico 93 US cells (New Mexico 45, Texas 34, Colorado 14) held until the 2024 keyframes took them back. This returns them from the start of the window; the cause is in p2000-p2009.

region.text: the ownerless land inside Iraq's frontiers (Salah ad-Din, Diyala, Ninawa): 84 cells that the islamic-state dossier left to nobody when its holdings ended

events.note: 'In late January 2015, Iraqi forces recaptured the entire province of Diyala'; the prime minister 'announced the end of the war' on 9 December 2017, after Kirkuk (October) and Al-Qa'im and Rawah (17 November 2017). The islamic-state dossier carries no loss for the rest of Salah ad-Din, Diyala and Ninawa, so these 84 cells passed to nobody when its keyframes ended and stayed ownerless from the 2020 anchor until the 2024 Cliopatria keyframe took them. Only ownerless cells move; the cause is in p2010-p2019.

region.text: the Uzbek-side cells of the one-cell band along the whole frontier that /ledger/4 gave to Kyrgyzstan

events.note: 'On November 17, 2022, Kyrgyzstan gained 156 km2 from Uzbekistan' (the frontier is 1,314 km long). /ledger/4 reads the 156 km2 as a one-cell band along the whole border, 34 cells (8,600 km2), so a strip of Uzbekistan is drawn Kyrgyz for 2022-2023. The 156 km2 is under one cell; this returns the strip to Uzbekistan.

region.text: the Kyrgyz-side cells of the one-cell border band that /ledger/5 gave to Uzbekistan

events.note: 'Until 2024, the Kyrgyz enclave of Barak existed in Uzbekistan'; the page gives no area. /ledger/5 reads the enclave as a one-cell band along the whole frontier, which took 36 Kyrgyz cells, and the 2024 Uzbek keyframe then threw them to nobody (a ring of ownerless cells in Jalal-Abad, Osh and Batken from 2024 on). The enclave is under one cell; this returns the band to Kyrgyzstan before the keyframe.
